questions.stem: Venice was built on islands in a lagoon at the head of the Adriatic Sea. How did this location help the Venetian Empire rise?
options: It cut the city off from the sea, so it relied on trade by land
It protected the city from land attack and opened sea routes east
It gave the city rich farmland that fed the whole of northern Italy
It placed the city on the main overland Silk Road from Beijing
questions.explanation: The shallow lagoon made Venice hard to attack from the mainland, while its position on the Adriatic linked it by sea to Constantinople, the Levant and Alexandria. Venice had little farmland and grew rich from maritime trade.

questions.stem: The Ottoman capture of Constantinople in 1453 gave the empire control of a city of great geo-strategic importance because it:
options: was the only city in the world able to produce the silk carried by traders
commanded the straits linking the Black Sea and the Mediterranean
was the main Atlantic port from which ships sailed to the Americas and West Africa
lay at the mouth of the Nile and controlled all of Egypt's grain exports
questions.explanation: Constantinople, renamed Istanbul, sits on the Bosporus, controlling sea traffic between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean and the land route between Europe and Asia. This made it a hub of trade and military power.

questions.stem: Portugal was a small kingdom with a long Atlantic coastline. Why did its geography encourage it to lead European exploration in the fifteenth century?
options: Its large population needed new farmland, which it could find in nearby France
Its mountains held the timber and silver needed to buy spices from the Ottomans
Facing the Atlantic, with land routes blocked by Castile, it looked to the sea
Its position on the Mediterranean gave it control of the spice trade with Venice
questions.explanation: Hemmed in by Castile on land, Portugal looked to the Atlantic, using its harbours, fishing traditions and knowledge of winds and currents to push down the coast of Africa. It had no Mediterranean coastline and a small population.

questions.stem: Russian expansion across Siberia from the late sixteenth century was made easier by:
options: a mild climate that let farmers settle quickly across the whole region
a chain of Ottoman ports along the coast of the Arctic Ocean
a network of Roman roads already built across northern Asia
long rivers and short overland portages that allowed travel by boat
questions.explanation: Siberia's great rivers and their tributaries, linked by short portages, let Cossacks and fur traders move east rapidly, building forts as they went. The climate was harsh, which is why settlement followed slowly behind the fur frontier.

questions.stem: For the Ming dynasty, which geographical challenge most shaped defence policy?
options: The Atlantic coast facing raids from Portuguese warships
The southern deserts facing attacks from Mughal cavalry
The western mountains facing invasion by the armies of the Russian tsars
The long northern frontier facing the peoples of the steppe
questions.explanation: The Ming had driven out the Mongol Yuan, and the open northern frontier remained their greatest security problem. This explains the huge rebuilding of the Great Wall in brick and stone under the Ming.

questions.stem: Which development most encouraged Portugal and Spain to seek a sea route to Asia in the fifteenth century?
options: The spice trade ran through Venetian and Ottoman-controlled middlemen
The Ming emperor had invited all European kingdoms to trade freely at Beijing
The Mughals had closed the land route through India to every European trader
A treaty with England gave Spain and Portugal sole rights to the Atlantic
questions.explanation: Spices and silks reached Europe through Muslim and Venetian intermediaries who took large profits. A direct sea route would cut out these middlemen. The Mughal Empire was not founded until 1526.

questions.stem: In 1415 Portugal began its overseas expansion by capturing:
options: Ceuta, in North Africa
Goa, on the coast of India
Malacca, on the Malay Peninsula
Salvador, on the coast of Brazil
questions.explanation: The capture of Ceuta, across the strait from Gibraltar, is usually taken as the start of Portugal's empire. Goa (1510) and Malacca (1511) were taken by Afonso de Albuquerque about a century later.

questions.stem: In 1492 Spain completed the conquest of Granada and sponsored Columbus's first voyage. How were these events connected?
options: Ending the Reconquista freed royal resources and crusading zeal for new ventures
Columbus had led the Spanish army that captured Granada from the Ottoman Turks
The fall of Granada closed Spain's ports, so Columbus had to sail from a Portuguese port
Granada's Muslim rulers paid for the voyage to escape from Spanish rule
questions.explanation: With the last Muslim kingdom in Iberia conquered, Isabella and Ferdinand could turn attention and resources outward, and the religious mission of the Reconquista carried over into the Americas. Granada was ruled by the Nasrid dynasty, not the Ottomans.

questions.stem: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) is significant to the rise of empires because it:
options: divided newly found lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal
ended the Seven Years' War and handed Canada and India to the British
gave the Dutch the right to trade with Japan from the island of Deshima
set the border between the Ottoman Empire and the Habsburgs at Vienna
questions.explanation: Spain and Portugal agreed a line in the Atlantic: lands to the west went to Spain, and lands to the east to Portugal, which is why Brazil became Portuguese. The Seven Years' War ended in 1763, much later.

questions.stem: Akbar expanded the Mughal Empire by force but also by marriage alliances with Rajput rulers and by giving them high rank. What was the main advantage of this policy?
options: It let the Rajputs choose the next emperor after Akbar's death
It turned powerful Hindu rivals into loyal partners in running the empire
It ended all warfare, so the Mughals no longer needed to keep an army at all
It made Hinduism the official religion of the Mughal court and empire
questions.explanation: By bringing Rajput princes into the imperial nobility, Akbar gained their military strength and loyalty, which helped him consolidate a vast, diverse empire. Akbar remained a Muslim ruler and fought many wars.

questions.stem: Ivan IV's conquest of the Khanate of Kazan in 1552 is seen as a turning point for Russia because it:
options: made Russia the ally of the Ottoman Empire against Persia
opened the Volga route for expansion south and east beyond Muscovy
gave Russia its first warm-water port on the Mediterranean Sea coast
ended Mongol rule over Moscow for the first time in its history
questions.explanation: Taking Kazan brought the middle Volga under Russian control and opened the way to Astrakhan, the Caspian and Siberia. Moscow had already thrown off Mongol overlordship in the fifteenth century.

questions.stem: The Qing dynasty took Beijing in 1644. Which circumstance best explains how the Manchus, a much smaller people, were able to conquer the Ming?
options: The Ming were weakened by revolt, and a Ming general let the Manchus through
The Ming had already surrendered to the Russians, who handed the empire to the Qing
The Manchus were invited by the Ming emperor to rule jointly with the Ming family
The Manchus arrived by sea with European guns bought from the Portuguese at Macau
questions.explanation: Peasant rebels under Li Zicheng took Beijing and the last Ming emperor took his own life. The Ming general Wu Sangui then allied with the Manchus, letting their banner armies through the Great Wall to defeat the rebels and claim the throne.

questions.stem: In the Ottoman devshirme system, the state:
options: sold Muslim prisoners of war to Venetian merchants to work in the galleys
forced every Ottoman subject to serve in the army for ten years before marriage
took Christian boys from the Balkans and trained them as soldiers or officials
allowed noble Turkish families to buy high offices in the government for their sons
questions.explanation: Devshirme recruits became Janissaries or palace officials, owing everything to the sultan rather than to family or region. Some rose to be grand viziers. This built a loyal elite and limited the power of the hereditary nobility.

questions.stem: The Ottoman millet system allowed:
options: European merchants to elect the governors of the provinces where they traded
every subject to choose freely whether to pay taxes to the sultan or the pope
non-Muslim communities to run many of their own affairs under their own leaders
only Sunni Muslims to live inside the walls of the Ottoman capital city of Istanbul
questions.explanation: Non-Muslim communities were organised under their religious leaders, who handled matters such as marriage, education and some law, in return for loyalty and taxes. This let a diverse empire be governed with limited conflict.

questions.stem: In Spain's American empire, people born in Spain (peninsulares) held most top offices, while American-born Spaniards (criollos) were often excluded. What does this show about imperial society?
options: Indigenous nobles held most of the senior posts in all of the American viceroyalties
The Crown let colonists elect the viceroys who governed the Americas
Birthplace and ancestry shaped status, creating resentment among colonial elites
All people of Spanish descent had equal access to every office in the empire
questions.explanation: A hierarchy based on birthplace and ancestry kept power with officials sent from Spain. Criollo resentment of this grew over time and later fed independence movements. Viceroys were appointed by the Crown.

questions.stem: Venetian identity was strongly linked to Saint Mark, whose relics, according to tradition, merchants brought from Alexandria in 828. This foundational story mattered because it:
options: gave the Doge the right to be crowned emperor in Constantinople
allowed Venice to claim the Nile Delta as part of its territory
gave the republic a patron saint and the prestige of an apostle's relics
proved that Venice had been founded by soldiers sent by the Ottoman sultan
questions.explanation: The winged lion of Saint Mark became the symbol of the republic, and the Basilica of San Marco housed his relics, giving Venice prestige and a distinct identity. The story did not create any claim to Egyptian territory.

questions.stem: Mercantilism is the economic theory that a nation's wealth is best increased by:
options: spending its bullion on imported luxury goods from Asia
exporting more than it imports and building up gold and silver
removing all tariffs on trade and letting the markets set prices freely
sharing colonies' resources equally with rival empires
questions.explanation: Mercantilists believed wealth was measured in bullion, so a state should run a trade surplus, protect home industry and use colonies as sources of raw materials and markets. Free trade was the later argument of Adam Smith.

questions.stem: The Dutch East India Company (VOC), founded in 1602, was a new kind of business because it:
options: traded only within Europe and never sent ships to Asia
raised capital by selling shares that investors could trade on an exchange
was owned entirely by the Dutch royal family and paid no dividends to anyone
was banned from using armed force or making treaties with rulers
questions.explanation: The VOC sold shares to many investors, traded on the Amsterdam exchange, so risk and profit were widely spread. It was also given the power to wage war, build forts and make treaties in Asia. The Dutch Republic had no royal family.

questions.stem: Why did the Venetian Arsenal give Venice such an advantage?
options: It was a state shipyard that built and fitted out galleys in great numbers
It was a bank that lent money to every European king at a low rate of interest
It was a fortress that guarded the land route from Venice to Vienna
It was a market where Venetians sold slaves from the Americas
questions.explanation: The Arsenal organised shipbuilding on an industrial scale, with standard parts and specialised workers, so Venice could produce merchant and war galleys quickly. This supported both trade and naval power.

questions.stem: In the late sixteenth century the Ming government began collecting taxes in silver rather than in goods and labour. Much of this silver came from:
options: Spanish mines in the Americas, shipped across the Pacific via Manila
British mines in India, shipped to Canton by the East India Company's fleet
Ottoman mines in Anatolia, carried overland on the Silk Road
Russian mines in Siberia, carried by sledge across the steppe
questions.explanation: Spanish galleons carried American silver from Acapulco to Manila, where it was traded for Chinese silk and porcelain. This linked the Ming economy to the Spanish Empire and to the global economy. The British East India Company had no Indian mines at that time.

questions.stem: Under Akbar, the Mughal zabt system of land revenue:
options: collected taxes only from Muslims and exempted all Hindu farmers
assessed tax on measured land and average crop yields, usually paid in cash
let every village decide for itself whether or not to pay any tax to the emperor
replaced all taxes with a single tribute paid by foreign merchants
questions.explanation: Developed with the minister Todar Mal, zabt measured land and set revenue on average yields and prices, giving the state a steady, predictable income. Akbar abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims, which would contradict the last option.

questions.stem: Prince Henry ‘the Navigator’ is significant to the Portuguese Empire because he:
options: sailed around the Cape of Good Hope in person
reached India by sea at Calicut in 1498
conquered Goa and made it the capital of Asia
sponsored voyages down the west coast of Africa
questions.explanation: Henry financed and organised expeditions that explored the African coast and Atlantic islands, although he did not sail on them himself. Dias rounded the Cape in 1488, da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, and Albuquerque took Goa.

questions.stem: Vasco da Gama's voyage of 1497–1499 was significant because it:
options: opened a direct sea route from Europe to India around Africa
was the first voyage to sail across the Pacific Ocean
claimed Brazil for Portugal after sailing west from Africa
found the Strait of Magellan at the tip of South America
questions.explanation: Da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, giving Portugal direct access to the spice trade. Cabral claimed Brazil in 1500, and Magellan's expedition found the strait and crossed the Pacific.

questions.stem: Afonso de Albuquerque built Portugal's power in Asia by:
options: settling thousands of Portuguese farmers on the plains of China
seizing key ports such as Goa, Malacca and Hormuz to control sea trade
conquering large inland territories across the whole of northern India
making peace with the Mughals and sharing the spice trade equally
questions.explanation: Albuquerque captured strategic ports that controlled sea lanes, creating a network of fortified bases rather than a land empire. Portugal's Asian empire remained small in territory and depended on naval power.

questions.stem: Zheng He led seven great voyages for the Ming between 1405 and 1433. Their main purpose was to:
options: conquer and settle colonies in East Africa and the Arabian Peninsula
find a sea route to Europe so the Ming could trade with Venice
search for gold mines on the islands of the Pacific Ocean
display Ming power and bring foreign rulers into the tribute system
questions.explanation: The treasure fleets sailed as far as East Africa, impressing rulers with Ming power and collecting tribute and exotic goods, such as a giraffe. They did not found colonies. The voyages ended after 1433.

questions.stem: Why did the Ming end Zheng He's voyages after 1433 rather than build on them?
options: The fleet was destroyed by the Portuguese navy in a battle off the coast of India
Zheng He had found that no other lands existed beyond the Indian Ocean
The Mughal emperor demanded that China stop sending ships into the Indian Ocean
Officials opposed their cost, and the northern frontier was the greater priority
questions.explanation: Confucian officials criticised the great expense, eunuch influence and lack of material return, while threats from the Mongols on the northern frontier absorbed resources. The Portuguese did not reach the Indian Ocean until 1498.

questions.stem: Peter the Great founded St Petersburg in 1703 on the Baltic coast. His main aim was to:
options: create a centre for the fur trade on the Pacific coast of Siberia
give Russia a port and a capital that looked towards Western Europe
move the capital closer to the Ottoman Empire to attack Istanbul
escape the cold of Moscow by building a city in the warm south
questions.explanation: St Petersburg, won from Sweden, gave Russia a ‘window on Europe’, a base for its new navy and a capital built in a Western style. It is in the north-west, far from the Ottomans and the Pacific.

questions.stem: The Ottoman sultan known in Turkish as ‘Kanuni’, the Lawgiver, for his legal reforms was:
options: Osman I
Selim I
Suleiman I
Mehmed II
questions.explanation: Suleiman I, called ‘the Magnificent’ in Europe, ruled from 1520 to 1566 and organised Ottoman law codes. Mehmed II conquered Constantinople, Osman I founded the dynasty, and Selim I conquered the Mamluk lands.

questions.stem: In the Venetian Republic, the Doge was elected for life but had limited personal power. Which institution held most political authority?
options: The Ottoman sultan, who confirmed each new Doge in office
The Great Council of noble families and the councils it elected
The Catholic pope, who appointed every Venetian official in Rome
An assembly of all the citizens, artisans and workers of Venice
questions.explanation: Venice was an oligarchy: the Great Council, limited to registered noble families after the Serrata of 1297, and smaller councils such as the Senate and the Council of Ten held power. Checks on the Doge prevented one-man rule.

questions.stem: Absolutism, as practised by Louis XIV of France, is best described as:
options: rule by the Catholic Church, with the king acting as the pope's governor
rule by a monarch who claims power from God and is not limited by a parliament
rule by an elected parliament that can remove the king if he breaks the nation's laws
rule by a council of merchants who appoint a king to lead the army in war
questions.explanation: Absolute monarchs claimed divine right and ruled without effective checks from representative bodies; Louis XIV did not call the Estates-General at all. Versailles displayed and centralised his authority over the nobility.

questions.stem: Akbar's mansabdari system organised the Mughal elite by:
options: appointing only Persian scholars to command the imperial armies
giving each officer a rank that set his pay and the cavalry he must supply
letting nobles pass their lands and titles to their sons without question
electing officers each year from among the leading merchant families
questions.explanation: Mansabdars held numbered ranks that fixed their salary, often from assigned land revenue, and the troops they maintained. Ranks were granted and could be removed by the emperor, binding the nobility to him.

questions.stem: Elizabeth I of England issued letters of marque to sea captains such as Francis Drake. This allowed them to:
options: found colonies in India under the control of the Mughal emperor
act as ambassadors to the Ottoman sultan in Istanbul
attack Spanish shipping legally and share the plunder with the Crown
trade freely in Spanish ports in the Americas without paying taxes
questions.explanation: Privateering, licensed piracy, let England weaken Spain and enrich investors and the Crown without the cost of a large state navy. Drake's raids on Spanish treasure ships were a major cause of tension before the Armada of 1588.

questions.stem: Both the Ming and the Qing used the tribute system in foreign relations. Which description is most accurate?
options: Foreign rulers elected the Chinese emperor in an assembly held at Beijing every ten years
Foreign rulers were forced to give up their thrones and become Chinese provincial governors
Foreign rulers sent envoys and gifts to honour the emperor, and got trade and gifts back
Foreign rulers paid most of their yearly tax income to China in exchange for military protection
questions.explanation: Tribute missions recognised the emperor's supremacy symbolically, and in return the court gave lavish gifts and access to trade. It expressed a Chinese view of the world with the emperor at the centre rather than direct rule over other states.

questions.stem: Martin Luther's challenge to the Catholic Church from 1517 affected the rivalry between empires mainly because:
options: it led the Ottoman sultan to convert to Lutheranism and to join the Holy Roman Empire
it made the pope the ruler of all the colonies claimed by Spain and Portugal
Protestant and Catholic states increasingly competed and fought, including overseas
it ended all religious wars in Europe and allowed empires to focus on trade alone
questions.explanation: The Reformation split Europe, and religion became part of imperial rivalry: Catholic Spain against Protestant England and the Dutch. The Catholic Counter-Reformation also drove missionary orders such as the Jesuits to Asia and the Americas.

questions.stem: Which religious order, founded in 1540, sent missionaries such as Francis Xavier and Matteo Ricci to Asia?
options: The Benedictines (Order of Saint Benedict)
The Knights Templar
The Lutheran Church
The Jesuits (Society of Jesus)
questions.explanation: The Society of Jesus, founded by Ignatius of Loyola, was central to the Counter-Reformation and worked in India, Japan, China and the Americas. Matteo Ricci adapted to Chinese culture at the Ming court.

questions.stem: Copernicus argued in 1543 that the earth moves around the sun. Why did ideas like this matter to the age of empires?
options: They showed that the Americas did not exist, which ended Spanish voyages westward
They valued observation and reason over received authority, aiding navigation
They proved the earth was flat, which encouraged sailors to stay close to the coast
They were accepted at once by the Church and became the basis of all imperial law
questions.explanation: The Scientific Revolution valued empirical observation and mathematics, which fed into astronomy, mapping and navigation used in imperial expansion. Educated Europeans already knew the earth was round, and the Church resisted heliocentrism.

questions.stem: Akbar's policy of sulh-i kul, often translated as ‘peace with all’, meant:
options: tolerance of different religions and an end to the tax on non-Muslims
the forced conversion of all Hindus in the empire to Sunni Islam
a promise never to fight any war against any neighbouring state
a ban on Persian culture at the Mughal court in favour of Turkish
questions.explanation: Akbar promoted religious tolerance, held debates between faiths at his court and abolished the jizya in 1564. This helped him rule an empire where most subjects were Hindu. Aurangzeb later reimposed the jizya.

questions.stem: The caravel helped the Portuguese explore the African coast because it:
options: was the largest ship of its age and could carry a thousand soldiers with ease
was driven by banks of oars and needed no wind to make headway
was built of iron, so it could not be damaged by coral reefs
was small and fast, and its lateen sails let it sail closer to the wind
questions.explanation: Caravels were light and manoeuvrable, and their triangular lateen sails allowed them to work against contrary winds, which was vital for returning from the African coast. Oared galleys were Mediterranean ships, and iron hulls came centuries later.

questions.stem: European navigators used the astrolabe and the quadrant mainly to find:
options: their longitude, by timing the sunset against a clock
the depth of the water, by dropping a weighted line
the direction of north, by using a magnetised needle
their latitude, by measuring the height of the sun or a star
questions.explanation: Measuring the angle of the sun or the Pole Star above the horizon gave latitude. Finding longitude reliably at sea had to wait for accurate marine chronometers in the eighteenth century, and the compass gave direction.

questions.stem: The Ottoman, Safavid and Mughal empires are sometimes called the ‘gunpowder empires’ because:
options: cannon and firearms helped them conquer and hold large territories
they invented gunpowder and kept the formula a secret from Europe
they banned firearms and relied on archers and cavalry instead
they grew rich by selling gunpowder to the Ming and the Qing
questions.explanation: Each made effective use of artillery and handguns: Mehmed II's cannons at Constantinople, and Babur's guns at Panipat in 1526. Gunpowder was invented in China, not by these empires.

questions.stem: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed in Europe around 1450, helped empires expand mainly because it:
options: ensured that only the clergy could read the books written about the Americas
spread maps, navigation guides and accounts of voyages quickly and cheaply
allowed governments to print paper money for the first time in history
replaced the need for ships by letting merchants trade through letters
questions.explanation: Printing multiplied copies of maps, sailing directions, travel accounts and religious texts, spreading knowledge and encouraging investment and exploration. Paper money had been used in China centuries earlier.

questions.stem: Which building was constructed as a cultural expression of imperial power after a conquest?
options: St Basil's Cathedral in Moscow, built after Ivan IV took Kazan
The Forbidden City in Beijing, built after the Ming fell to the Qing
The Taj Mahal in Agra, built after Babur's victory at Panipat
The Palace of Versailles, built after France conquered Spain
questions.explanation: Ivan IV commissioned St Basil's to celebrate the capture of Kazan in 1552. The Forbidden City was built by the Ming, the Taj Mahal was a tomb built by Shah Jahan for his wife, and France never conquered Spain.

questions.stem: The architect Sinan, who designed the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul, expressed Ottoman power by:
options: designing palaces in the Gothic style copied from the churches of Venice
building the first skyscrapers of the Islamic world for the sultan
rebuilding the walls of Constantinople after their total collapse
building great domed mosques that rivalled the Byzantine Hagia Sophia
questions.explanation: Sinan's mosques, with vast domes and slender minarets, presented the sultan as a pious and powerful ruler who surpassed the Byzantines whose city he now ruled. They were part of large complexes with schools, hospitals and kitchens.

questions.stem: Every year on Ascension Day the Doge of Venice sailed into the Adriatic and dropped a ring into the water in the ceremony known as the Marriage of the Sea. What did this festival express?
options: Venice's claim to rule the sea, which was the source of its wealth and power
Venice's surrender of the Adriatic to the Ottoman navy after a defeat
Venice's wish to give up trade at sea and become a farming state on the mainland
Venice's alliance with Portugal to share control of the Atlantic Ocean
questions.explanation: The ceremony symbolised a marriage between Venice and the sea, asserting Venetian dominion over the Adriatic. Such festivals reinforced civic identity and displayed imperial power to citizens and foreign visitors.
